description: Schedule, start, monitor, and stop drip zones, center pivots, well pumps, and fertigation injection through the SCADA system (Farms 1 and 2) and the pivot manufacturer's cloud service (Farm 3), using FMIS irrigation schedules
process_owner: Director of Irrigation and Water Resources
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Plastic-mulch beds on drip need water every day in spring heat; a missed day stresses about 3,600 acres of vegetables and 1,100 acres of berries; fertigation timing affects yield; schedules and setpoints change daily, so RPO is 1 hour
source_evidence: EV-066 (Director of Irrigation and Water Resources interview); EV-039 (Hand-Off-Auto panels; Farm 3 manual procedure); EV-014 (54 wells, 14 skids)
manual_workaround: Irrigation Technicians run pumps and injection skids by hand at each panel (Hand-Off-Auto switches) from a printed schedule; 12 technicians can cover about half of the 54 wells per shift; Farm 3 has written manual pivot procedures, Farms 1 and 2 do not
dependent_systems: SYS-07 (SCADA, PLCs, pivots, valves, sensors); SYS-05; SYS-01 irrigation module; SYS-04 farm data hub
dependent_third_parties: SCADA integrator; pivot manufacturer cloud service; FMIS vendor; electric utility; cellular carrier
dependent_people_or_facilities: Irrigation Technicians; Irrigation Operations Center; pump stations at Farms 1-3
quantified_operational_impact: About 4,700 irrigated crop acres; each day without scheduled irrigation in April to May heat costs an estimated 2% to 4% of the affected crop
quantified_regulatory_impact: Monthly water use reports need complete flow meter data; fertigation over-application can breach label rates and permit conditions
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: incorrect fertigation or manual chemical handling exposes Irrigation Technicians to concentrated fertilizer
regulatory_driver: CSF 2.0 GV.OC-04 (benchmark); SP 800-82r3 5.3.2; N11-R01 (21 CFR 121.130 used as a voluntary checklist for fertigation)

description: Start overhead irrigation on 700 acres of strawberries before the canopy reaches the critical temperature on freeze nights, from weather station alarms and SCADA pump starts
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A failed or late start on a freeze night damages blooms and fruit within about 2 hours; about 6 to 12 freeze nights a season (December to February); setpoints change rarely, so RPO is 24 hours
source_evidence: EV-066 (Farm 2 Farm Manager interview); EV-040 (single alarm dialer); EV-039 (no written night-start procedure)
manual_workaround: Freeze-night crew of 4 Irrigation Technicians starts the 14 Farm 2 pumps by hand from a standalone thermometer alarm; procedure unwritten and untested (EV-039)
dependent_systems: SYS-07 (Farm 2 pumps, weather stations, SCADA alarm dialer); SYS-05 (radio link)
dependent_third_parties: Electric utility; SCADA integrator; weather data provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Farm 2 Irrigation Technicians on call; Farm Manager
quantified_operational_impact: Up to 700 acres affected; a full failed night can cost 2 to 3 weeks of harvest (estimated $1.5 million to $2 million worst case)
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: technicians working at pump stations at night in freezing conditions

business_process: Harvest planning, crew dispatch, and field tally
description: Plan daily harvest by block, dispatch crews, and record field tally (piece-rate counts by worker) and harvest traceability data on crew lead tablets in SYS-01
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Harvest cannot be delayed more than about half a day without fruit loss; field tally is the H-2A earnings record and the first traceability record, so entries must not be lost (RPO 1 hour)
source_evidence: EV-066 (Farm Managers interview); EV-049 (FMIS vendor RTO 8 hours, RPO 1 hour); EV-007 (crew tablets)
manual_workaround: Paper tally cards in English and Spanish signed by crew leads and keyed in later; harvest by the prior day's plan
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (mobile app and web); SYS-06 crew lead tablets; SYS-05 (cellular and farm Wi-Fi); SYS-02
dependent_people_or_facilities: 60 crew leads; up to 370 H-2A workers; Farm Managers
quantified_operational_impact: About 9,000 to 14,000 tally entries a day at peak; keying from paper takes about 3 office staff 1 day per harvest day
quantified_regulatory_impact: H-2A earnings records must be accurate and adequate (20 CFR 655.122(j)(1)); harvest records under the Produce Safety Rule (21 CFR 112.161)

description: Receive bins, run 4 packing lines with optical graders, forced-air cool, ripen tomatoes with ethylene, label lots, and hold product in cold storage
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Strawberries and blueberries lose shelf life within hours without cooling; ripening rooms need controlled ethylene and temperature; about $490,000 of shipments per day depend on it
source_evidence: EV-066 (Packinghouse Manager interview); EV-062 (about $490,000 of shipments per shipping day); EV-063 (packinghouse volume)
manual_workaround: Run lines in manual mode with hand grading; manual cooling tunnel and room setpoints at the local controllers; hand-applied lot labels from pre-printed stock
dependent_systems: SYS-07 (packing line PLCs, graders, cooling and ripening controls); SYS-05 (packinghouse); SYS-01; SYS-10
dependent_third_parties: Refrigeration service contractor; packing line vendor; grader vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 9,000 packages an hour across 4 lines at peak; hand grading drops throughput by about 60%
quantified_regulatory_impact: Lot codes and pack records support Produce Safety and traceability records; retail customer notice within 24 hours of events affecting committed volumes (contract)
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: ethylene and refrigeration systems have their own hardwired safety shutoffs; manual operation raises worker exposure
regulatory_driver: CSF 2.0 GV.OC-04 (benchmark); SP 800-82r3 5.3.1; N11-R01 (21 CFR 121.130 used as a voluntary checklist for ripening rooms)

description: Monitor 140 temperature sensors in cooling tunnels, ripening rooms, cold storage, and trailers; page staff on excursions; keep temperature logs for customers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A cooler excursion that is not seen within about 2 hours can spoil a room of berries (up to about $40,000) and send unsafe product; logs are customer records
source_evidence: EV-066 (Packinghouse Manager interview); EV-040 (cold-chain alarm service)
manual_workaround: Hourly manual temperature rounds with paper logs; standalone thermometers in each room
dependent_systems: SYS-07 (sensors, alarm service); SYS-05; SYS-14 (none today)
dependent_third_parties: Cold-chain alarm service vendor; refrigeration contractor
quantified_operational_impact: Up to 12 ripening rooms and 6 cold rooms monitored; manual rounds take 1 person per shift
quantified_regulatory_impact: Customer temperature records; product hold and recall decisions depend on complete logs
safety_impact_detail: Severe: undetected temperature abuse can send unsafe produce to retail

description: Receive retail and foodservice orders by EDI, allocate product, build loads, print bills of lading, send advance ship notices, and invoice
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Retail delivery windows are fixed; missed windows bring chargebacks and lost programs; about $490,000 of shipments per shipping day
source_evidence: EV-066 (Director of Sales interview); EV-062 (shipments per shipping day); EV-056 (delivery windows and chargebacks)
manual_workaround: Phone and email orders from the top 10 customers; manual bills of lading from templates; EDI messages re-sent after recovery
dependent_systems: SYS-10 (ERP and EDI); SYS-02; SYS-03; SYS-06
dependent_third_parties: ERP vendor; EDI network provider; carriers
quantified_operational_impact: About 45 truckloads a week at peak; manual order entry handles about 60% of normal volume
quantified_regulatory_impact: Retail supplier agreements: notice within 24 hours of events affecting committed volumes (contract)

business_process: Traceability, lot coding, and recall support
description: Assign lot codes at initial packing, link harvest field, packing, and shipping records, run mock recalls, and answer customer or FDA trace-back requests
process_owner: Director of Food Safety and Quality
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Trace-back requests from customers or FDA must be answered within 24 hours; lot links must not be lost
source_evidence: EV-066 (Director of Food Safety and Quality interview); EV-043 (mock recalls); EV-056 (traceability terms)
manual_workaround: Lot codes from pre-printed label stock; paper receiving and shipping logs; trace from bills of lading
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-10; SYS-07 (packing line labelers); SYS-04 (farm data hub)
quantified_operational_impact: A trace-back across one week of tomatoes covers about 1,800 lots from 40 fields and 12 growers
quantified_regulatory_impact: Produce Safety records on FDA request within 24 hours when offsite (21 CFR 112.166(a)); Food Traceability Rule records in an electronic sortable spreadsheet within 24 hours when FDA requests (21 CFR 1.1455(c)(3)(ii); not enforced before 2028-07-20)
safety_impact_detail: Severe: a slow or incomplete trace widens a recall and delays removal of unsafe product

business_process: Produce Safety and pesticide application records
description: Record and display pesticide application and hazard information, worker training, agricultural water, cleaning and sanitizing, and harvest records in SYS-01 and on farm display boards
process_owner: Director of Food Safety and Quality
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Pesticide application information must be displayed within 24 hours after an application ends (40 CFR 170.311(b)(5)); records must be created at the time of the activity (21 CFR 112.161(a)(2))
source_evidence: EV-066 (Director of Food Safety and Quality interview); EV-051 (records held in SYS-01)
manual_workaround: Paper application and food safety forms from the field binder; display board updated by hand
quantified_operational_impact: About 40 pesticide applications a week in season across 3 farms
quantified_regulatory_impact: WPS display and 2-year retention (40 CFR 170.311(b)); Produce Safety records (21 CFR 112 Subpart O); third-party audit findings
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: workers need application and restricted-entry information to avoid exposure

description: Auto-steer planting, bed shaping, and spraying from the RTK network; variable-rate and section-control prescriptions; camera-based targeted spraying (AI-003); as-applied data back to SYS-01
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Planting and spraying windows are a few days; manual steering is slower and less precise
source_evidence: EV-066 (Precision Agriculture Manager interview); EV-010 (85 machines; 3 RTK base stations)
manual_workaround: Manual steering with foam markers; broadcast spraying at label rates instead of targeted spraying; paper as-applied records
dependent_third_parties: Equipment dealer; GNSS correction services; telematics portal vendor
quantified_operational_impact: 85 machines; manual steering cuts field efficiency by about 20%; broadcast spraying raises chemical use
quantified_regulatory_impact: Pesticide application records (40 CFR 170.311(b)); label rates
safety_impact_detail: Moderate: broadcast spraying increases chemical use and handler exposure

business_process: Crop scouting, drone imagery, and yield forecasting
description: Fly weekly imagery missions, run computer-vision yield estimates (AI-001), and feed harvest and sales planning
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Weekly forecasts; planning can use the prior week's estimate and hand counts
source_evidence: EV-066 (Precision Agriculture Manager interview); EV-065 (yield model)
manual_workaround: Hand counts on sample plots; prior-week estimates
dependent_systems: SYS-09; SYS-04 (imagery data lake); agronomy analytics SaaS
quantified_operational_impact: Forecast accuracy falls back to hand counts

business_process: Grower irrigation monitoring and agronomy alerts
description: Collect soil probe and flow data from 18 contract growers, send irrigation alerts and recommended schedules through the grower portal
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Growers rely on daily alerts in heat; service terms promise 99.5% monthly availability in season
source_evidence: EV-066 (Vice President of Grower Services interview); EV-057 (99.5% monthly availability term)
manual_workaround: Phone and text alerts from the agronomy team using vendor dashboards
dependent_systems: SYS-12; SYS-04; SYS-07 (grower probes via LoRaWAN and cellular); SYS-02
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider; development firm; cellular carrier
quantified_operational_impact: 18 growers, about 2,700 acres; agronomists can phone about 6 growers a day

business_process: Grower pack-out reporting and pool settlement
description: Compute weekly pool settlements from pack-out by grade, sales prices, and charges; post statements to the grower portal; pay growers by ACH
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Statements post every Tuesday and payments go out Wednesday; lenders and growers depend on the schedule; about $900,000 a week
source_evidence: EV-066 (Vice President of Grower Services interview); EV-063 (about $900,000 a week); EV-057 (settlement schedule)
manual_workaround: Controller calculates settlements in a spreadsheet from ERP and pack-out exports; statements by email
quantified_operational_impact: About 30 growers settled weekly; manual calculation takes 2 analysts 2 days
quantified_regulatory_impact: Marketing agreements set payment dates; errors must be corrected and reported to growers (contract)

business_process: Payroll, H-2A earnings statements, and timekeeping
description: Collect time from biometric clocks and field tally, run weekly payroll, and give each H-2A worker an earnings statement on or before payday
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Weekly payday; H-2A statements are required on or before each payday
source_evidence: EV-066 (HR Director interview); EV-003 (up to 370 H-2A workers)
manual_workaround: Repeat prior week's payroll for salaried staff; manual hours and piece-rate from paper tally; printed statements
quantified_operational_impact: Up to 600 paychecks a week at peak
quantified_regulatory_impact: Earnings statements on or before each payday (20 CFR 655.122(k)); earnings records (655.122(j))

description: Compile monthly withdrawals per well from flow meter data and file permit reports
process_owner: Director of Irrigation and Water Resources
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Monthly report; flow history must not be lost (RPO 24 hours)
source_evidence: EV-066 (Director of Irrigation and Water Resources interview); EV-059 (water use permit conditions)
manual_workaround: Manual meter readings at each well
dependent_systems: SYS-07 (flow meters, historian); SYS-04 (farm data hub)

description: Pay vendors, apply customer payments, manage cash and the credit line
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Weekly payment runs; cash collection from retail customers
source_evidence: EV-066 (Chief Financial Officer interview); EV-061 (payment approvals)
manual_workaround: Bank portal payments for critical vendors; manual cash application
quantified_operational_impact: About $1.8 million of payables a week in season

business_process: Direct retail sales (on-farm market, U-pick, online pre-orders)
description: Sell at the Farm 2 market and U-pick, and take online pre-orders and U-pick bookings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $2 million a year, mostly weekends in season
source_evidence: EV-066 (Director of Sales interview); EV-062 (about $2 million direct retail)
manual_workaround: Cash only at the market; walk-in U-pick without bookings

business_process: USDA program, crop insurance, and acreage reporting
description: File acreage and production reports and keep program records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Deadlines are seasonal and known weeks ahead
source_evidence: EV-066 (Controller interview); EV-059 (USDA program and crop insurance documents)
manual_workaround: Prepare from paper and ERP exports
dependent_third_parties: Crop insurance agent; USDA service center
quantified_regulatory_impact: Program deadlines (missed acreage reports can affect coverage)

description: Email, files, chat, and single sign-on for all office users
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Most coordination and customer communication runs through email and chat
source_evidence: EV-066 (IT Director interview); EV-001 (identity provider export)
manual_workaround: Out-of-band messaging group on phones; phone trees
